c.tagline: The walled 'City of Popes,' with a monumental Gothic palace and the legendary broken Pont Saint-Bénézet

card: Widely accepted; cash useful for small market stalls

taxi.fare: Metered, roughly €3.50 flag fall plus per-km rate
taxi.fareNote: Metered fares are standard and reliable

emergency.note: 112 is the general EU-style emergency number that connects to police, fire, and ambulance

walk: The walled old town is compact and entirely walkable; a car or bus is useful for day trips into Provence

safety.safety: Very safe city, popular with visitors of all ages
safety.crime: Petty theft near the Palais des Papes and train station is the main concern

hood_landmark.Intra-Muros (Walled Old Town): The Palais des Papes and Place de l'Horloge
hood_landmark.Pont Saint-Bénézet Area: The Pont Saint-Bénézet bridge over the Rhône
hood_landmark.Rocher des Doms: The Rocher des Doms garden overlooking the Rhône
hood_landmark.Les Halles / Market District: Les Halles d'Avignon covered food market
hood_landmark.Île de la Barthelasse: The Île de la Barthelasse riverside park island

avoid.reason: The Monclar and Rocade housing estates south of the train station are best avoided at night.
Pickpockets target festival crowds in July and the area around the train station after dark.

hood_desc: The entire historic city within its medieval ramparts, home to the Palais des Papes and most restaurants and hotels; the natural base for any visit.
The riverfront area around the famous half-bridge, popular for photos and river walks at sunset.
A hilltop garden just north of the Palais des Papes with sweeping views over the Rhône and Villeneuve-lès-Avignon.
The market quarter with Les Halles and a lively cafe scene, good for food-focused visitors.
A rural river island just across the Rhône, offering cycling paths, farms, and a quiet green escape from the walled city.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink, as throughout France.

transit.sys: Orizo (formerly TCRA) urban bus and tram network
transit.pay: Cash or contactless card on board; rechargeable travel card available
transit.note: The walled old town is pedestrian-friendly; buses mainly serve outlying neighborhoods and the TGV station

transport.air: Avignon-Provence Airport (AVN) has limited flights; Marseille Provence (MRS) is a larger option about 1 hr away
transport.train: TGV high-speed rail connects Avignon to Paris (under 3 hr) and Marseille
transport.bus: Regional buses connect to Luberon villages and other Provence towns
transport.car: Well connected via the A7 motorway; the old town is best explored on foot

airport.name: Marseille Provence Airport (main regional gateway)
airport.transport: Train via Marseille Saint-Charles, or rental car

net.w: Free wifi standard in hotels and cafes
net.ap: An Orange, SFR, or Bouygues tourist SIM or eSIM

tip.s: Not obligatory; rounding up is appreciated for guides and tours
tip.r: Service is included by law; rounding up is a nice gesture, not expected
